description: Render an HTML string to a PDF with a headless browser, so layout, CSS (flexbox, grid, print styles), images and web fonts come out as in a browser print. It takes HTML text only: there is no URL input, and JavaScript is switched off, so scripts do not run and pages that build themselves with JavaScript render empty. External resources (images, stylesheets, fonts) load only over https from public hosts; anything else (http, file, private or internal addresses, redirects to them) is blocked and skipped, and the PDF is still made. Data URIs work and are the safest way to include images. Letter or A4, portrait or landscape, margin in points (default 36), backgrounds printed by default, optional scale. html is capped at 1 MB, the document at 50 pages and 16 MB, external resources at 50 requests and 40 MB, and rendering at 15 seconds. Frames, iframes, objects, embeds, audio and video are not rendered, and an inline or fetched image is decoded and checked first. Common fonts (Helvetica, Arial, Times, Courier and generic families) render as Liberation faces, metric-compatible with the originals. Once the renderer is reached every outcome costs 5 of your monthly request quota, not 1, failures included; a cheap refusal before a browser starts (for example an inline image refused: image_too_large or unsupported_image, with the image named in the message) costs 1; only input validation errors and a busy or unreachable renderer cost nothing. Images: 16 megapixels at most each (96 in total), PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG (simplified: scripts, style sheets, filters, masks, embedded images and links are removed; inline style colours are kept); AVIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF, animated PNG and colour-bitmap fonts are not supported, and an image in an unsupported format or over a limit fails the request (a missing image, such as a 404 or a tracking pixel, is skipped). Returns the PDF inline as an application/pdf resource, up to 4,000,000 bytes (larger results fail with an error pointing to POST /api/html-to-pdf, which streams up to 16 MB). For Markdown, text or CSV with no HTML use pdf_text_to_pdf; to build an invoice from data use pdf_invoice.
